candidates.title: Index incoming school documents

ease.reason: A spreadsheet can hold a proposed document index, but formats and filing rules are absent from the notice.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: schools may value less document handling; this vacancy establishes human work, not AI-service demand.

feasibility.reason: A two-week mock can index synthetic files, while archive rules and real-system access remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: The index can be drafted repeatedly, but a clerk must classify, verify and file each document.

evidence.reason: The fresh paid notice names incoming post and school-document archiving, but gives no fields or process details.

candidates.reason: Proposed experiment: each operator-supplied fictional document triggers an index draft; a clerk checks its category and date, then files it manually. No attached building reference supports school-document classification; mean 4.6, below 6.

demandEvidence.chore: Index operator-supplied fictional incoming school documents for a clerk to verify before filing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: hantering av post och inkommande dokument arkivering och hantering av skolans dokument

candidates.title: Review a fictional student schedule

ease.reason: A spreadsheet mock can compare supplied schedule rows; the notice gives no fields or adjustment rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: school offices may value schedule checks; the vacancy does not establish AI-service buyers.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic-row checker is a plausible two-week experiment; real systems and authorization are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable check can flag possible conflicts, but staff must interpret needs and approve schedules.

evidence.reason: The paid notice names schedule updates and individual schedules, but not validation rules or outcomes.

candidates.reason: Proposed experiment: importing fictional schedule rows triggers possible-conflict flags; staff check them against operator-supplied rules and approve changes. No attached reference supports school validation; mean 4.6, below 6.

demandEvidence.chore: Flag possible conflicts in fictional individual-schedule rows for a school administrator to review.

candidates.title: Check fictional school timetable rows

ease.reason: A spreadsheet mock can compare supplied timetable rows; the notice does not provide columns or rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: school offices may value fewer timetable checks; AI-service purchases are not evidenced.

feasibility.reason: A narrow conflict flagger can use synthetic rows in two weeks; actual school-system access is unknown.

autonomy.reason: Repeated comparison can flag rows, but staff must interpret conflicts and approve any schedule change.

evidence.reason: The paid notice lists timetable and teaching-group administration, but not a specific validation workflow.

candidates.reason: Proposed experiment: a fictional timetable batch triggers conflict flags; staff compare them with operator-supplied rules and approve any change. No attached reference supports school validation; mean 4.6, below 6.

demandEvidence.chore: Flag possible timetable-row conflicts in fictional or operator-supplied test data for staff review.

candidates.title: Prepare an invoice review sheet

ease.reason: The attached n8n example lists PDF invoice field extraction and sheet logging; it does not establish school coding rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: school offices may value invoice preparation; a paid human vacancy does not prove AI-tool demand.

feasibility.reason: A fictional-PDF extraction and review sheet is a plausible two-week test; no school system integration is shown.

autonomy.reason: The example supports intake, extraction and logging; a person must verify coding and make every approval decision.

evidence.reason: The vacancy names invoice handling and the separate example describes extraction, but neither shows school use or outcomes.

candidates.reason: Proposed experiment: each fictional PDF triggers field extraction into a review sheet; a clerk checks values and decides coding and approval. The attached example supports extraction/logging only; mean 5.2, below 6, with no new evidence changing recent related refusals.

demandEvidence.chore: Extract proposed invoice fields from fictional PDFs into a review sheet; staff verify coding and approval.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: löneadministration och hantering av fakturor (kontering och attest) samt vikarieanskaffning utifrån behov

candidates.title: Draft an order and delivery checklist

ease.reason: A spreadsheet can hold a checklist, but the notice supplies no order fields or status rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a school office may value order tracking; the notice establishes no AI-service demand.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic order checklist can be tested in two weeks, while actual supplier and library systems are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A draft checklist can be repeated, but staff must confirm delivery status and update official records.

evidence.reason: The paid notice names orders, deliveries and mail, but gives no fields, frequency or process.

candidates.reason: Proposed experiment: each fictional order note triggers a delivery checklist; a clerk checks status and updates official records. No attached building reference supports this workflow; its modest prototype scores 4.6, below 6.

demandEvidence.chore: Turn fictional order and delivery notes into a review checklist for school office staff.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Du hanterar beställningar, leveranser och post Du registrerar elever och böcker i vårt utlåningssystem

candidates.title: Draft answers to timetable questions

ease.reason: A mock can sort sample questions using a supplied FAQ, but the notice provides no fields or school guidance.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: school offices may value help with recurring schedule questions; AI-service demand is unproved.

feasibility.reason: A small sample-based drafting test is feasible, but internal calendars and policy access are unknown.

autonomy.reason: Drafting is repeatable, but staff must verify schedule facts and send any answer.

evidence.reason: The paid notice names scheduling and schedule questions, but does not describe their frequency or answers.

candidates.reason: Proposed experiment: each fictional question triggers an FAQ-based reply draft; staff check calendar facts and send it. This duplicates recent post e20bcacf021524725d3fc275, which triages questions and drafts replies; mean 4.6.

demandEvidence.chore: Sort fictional timetable questions and draft replies from operator-supplied approved guidance for staff review.
